# VIC-20 (Iteration 2) Implementation Brief

Canonical native tree: `F:\GitHub\vice-sharp\native\vice\vice\src\vic20\` and ROMs under `native\vice\vice\data\VIC20\`. Managed TODO: `PLAN-ARCHVIC20-001` (see `HANDOFF.md`). Roadmap: VIC-I 6560/6561 in `docs/Iteration-Roadmap.md`.

---

## 1. Native VIC-20 layout (VICE)

### 1.1 Memory map

Source: `vic20mem.c` `mem_initialize_memory` and block flags in `vic20mem.h`.

| Region | Range | Content |
|--------|-------|---------|
| ZP / low RAM | `$0000-$03FF` | Always RAM (1 KB; ZP separate table entry) |
| BLK0 / RAM123 | `$0400-$0FFF` | Optional 3 KB expansion (`VIC_BLK0`) or cart RAM123 |
| Internal | `$1000-$1FFF` | Always RAM (4 KB; total unexpanded = 5 KB) |
| BLK1 | `$2000-$3FFF` | Optional 8 KB RAM / cart |
| BLK2 | `$4000-$5FFF` | Optional 8 KB RAM / cart |
| BLK3 | `$6000-$7FFF` | Optional 8 KB RAM / cart |
| CHAR ROM | `$8000-$8FFF` | Chargen (4 KB, read-only) |
| I/O0 | `$9000-$93FF` | VIC + VIA1 + VIA2 (decode below) |
| Color RAM | `$9400-$97FF` | 1K × 4-bit color RAM (VICE maps into RAM image) |
| I/O2 | `$9800-$9BFF` | Expansion I/O |
| I/O3 | `$9C00-$9FFF` | Expansion I/O |
| BLK5 | `$A000-$BFFF` | Optional 8 KB RAM / cart (often cart autostart) |
| BASIC | `$C000-$DFFF` | 8 KB BASIC ROM |
| KERNAL | `$E000-$FFFF` | 8 KB KERNAL ROM |

Block flags (`vic20mem.h:41-46`): `VIC_BLK0=1`, `BLK1=2`, `BLK2=4`, `BLK3=8`, `BLK5=16`. Cart overlay bits: `VIC_CART_RAM123` / `BLK1` / `BLK2` / `BLK3` / `BLK5` / `IO2` / `IO3`.

Unconnected expansion reads use lingering C-bus data (`vic20_cpu_last_data`); V-bus side-effects apply on `$0000-$1FFF` and `$8000-$9FFF` (`vic20mem.h:78-90`).

### 1.2 I/O decode (VIC / VIA1 / VIA2)

From `vic20.c:301-449`:

| Device | Canonical base | Select bit | Interrupt |
|--------|----------------|------------|-----------|
| **VIC-I** | `$9000` (window `$9000-$90FF`, 16 regs mirrored) | always in I/O0 | none (no raster IRQ) |
| **VIA1** | `$9110` | **A4** set | **NMI** (`IK_NMI`, `vic20via1.c:291`) |
| **VIA2** | `$9120` | **A5** set | **IRQ** (`IK_IRQ`, `vic20via2.c:249`) |

Reads/writes can hit multiple devices; values are AND-combined (`vic_via1_via2_read`). Skeleton can use clean bases `$9000` / `$9110` / `$9120` with 16-byte mirrors first; full A4/A5 mirror windows later.

### 1.3 VIA1 roles (`vic20via1.c`, `vic20iec.c`)

- **NMI** source.
- **Port A** (`read_pra` / `store_pra`, ~221-252):
  - bit 0: IEC **CLK in**
  - bit 1: IEC **DATA in**
  - bits 2-5: joystick up/down/left/fire
  - bit 6: tape sense (also userport-related)
  - bit 7: IEC **ATN out**
- Port B: userport PB (+ VFLI color-RAM address hack on PB0-3).
- PCR: tape motor on CA2-related bits; userport PA2 on CB2.
- Light pen via joy/PA fire path into `vic_set_light_pen`.

### 1.4 VIA2 roles (`vic20via2.c`, `vic20iec.c`)

- **IRQ** source (keyboard timers, etc.).
- **Keyboard**: Port B columns (write), Port A rows (read); matrix documented `vic20via2.c:148-171`. PB7 also joystick **right**.
- PB3: cassette write.
- **PCR / IEC** (`vic20iec.c:129-137`, `iec_pcr_write`):
  - VIA2 **CA2** = IEC **CLK out**
  - VIA2 **CB2** = IEC **DATA out**
  - VIA2 **CB1** = IEC **SRQ in**
  - VIA1 PA carries ATN out + CLK/DATA in

This is **not** the C64 CIA2 PA wiring; host IEC for VIC-20 must be a dedicated board glue device.

### 1.5 VIC-I (6560 NTSC / 6561 PAL) registers

16 registers at `$9000+$0..$F` (`vic-mem.c`, `victypes.h:169` `regs[0x10]`):

| Offset | Function |
|--------|----------|
| `$0` | Screen X origin |
| `$1` | Screen Y origin |
| `$2` | Columns (bits 0-6); bit 7 is video matrix address bit |
| `$3` | Rows (bits 1-6), raster bit 0, char height 8/16 (bit 0) |
| `$4` | Raster line (read-only) |
| `$5` | Video matrix + char base |
| `$6/$7` | Light pen X/Y |
| `$8/$9` | Paddle X/Y |
| `$A-$D` | Bass / Alto / Soprano / Noise (freq + enable) |
| `$E` | Aux color (high nibble) + master volume (low) |
| `$F` | Background (high nibble), reverse (bit 3 inverted), border (low 3 bits) |

Default text grid ~22×23; PAL max text cols 32, NTSC 31 (`victypes.h:35-36`). VIC-I is **video + 4-voice audio** (no SID).

### 1.6 PAL vs NTSC

From `vic20.h` and `vic-timing.h` / `vic-timing.c`:

| | PAL (6561) | NTSC (6560) |
|--|------------|-------------|
| CPU clock | 1 108 405 Hz | 1 022 727 Hz |
| Cycles/line | **71** | **65** |
| Screen lines | **312** | **261** (comment: really 262, first+last share a line) |
| Cycle offset | 0 | 37 |
| Full pixel width | 284 (= 71×4) | 260 (= 65×4) |
| Normal display width | 224 | 200 |
| Normal first/last displayed line | 28 / 311 | 28 / 261 |
| Pixel doubling | VIC_PIXEL_WIDTH 2 | same |
| Default kernal | `kernal.901486-07.bin` | `kernal.901486-06.bin` |

Models (`vic20model.c:56-61`): PAL, NTSC, SuperVIC (NTSC + BLK1|BLK2), VIC-1001 Japanese (NTSC + JP chargen/kernal).

### 1.7 ROM filenames (VICE data/VIC20 + DRIVES)

From `vic20rom.h` and `data/VIC20/Makefile.am`:

| Role | Filename | Size |
|------|----------|------|
| BASIC | `basic-901486-01.bin` | 8 KB (`0x2000`) |
| KERNAL PAL (default) | `kernal.901486-07.bin` | 8 KB |
| KERNAL NTSC | `kernal.901486-06.bin` | 8 KB |
| KERNAL JP | `kernal.901486-02.bin` | 8 KB |
| Chargen (default) | `chargen-901460-03.bin` | 4 KB (`0x1000`) |
| Chargen JP | `chargen-901460-02.bin` | 4 KB |
| DOS 1540 | `dos1540-325302+3-01.bin` under `DRIVES/` | 16 KB |

Note: VIC-20 kernals use a **dot** after `kernal`, not a dash (`ViceRomCatalog.cs:57-61`).

---

## 2. Existing managed reuse

### 2.1 `Mos6502` without 6510 I/O port

- Single class: `src/ViceSharp.Chips/Cpu/Mos6502.cs`. No separate `Mos6510`.
- `HandlesAddress` always **false** (`Mos6502.cs:1467`): CPU does **not** own `$00/$01`.
- C64 processor port lives in **PLA / `C64MemoryMap`**, not the CPU.
- Drive machines already use plain `new Mos6502(bus)` (`ArchitectureBuilder.cs:255`).
- **VIC-20**: same pattern. IRQ via `SystemClock` + `InterruptLine(Irq)`; NMI via second line + `Mos6502.Nmi()` (`Mos6502.cs:130-138`). Wire VIA1 → NMI, VIA2 → IRQ.
- Optional later: cycle-accurate NMI sequence (current `Nmi()` is multi-cycle push in one call).

### 2.2 `Via6522` public API for board callbacks

`src/ViceSharp.Chips/IEC/Via6522.cs`:

| Surface | Lines | Use on VIC-20 |
|---------|-------|----------------|
| `BaseAddress`, `Size` | 136-139 | `$9110` / `$9120`, size `0x10` (or larger mirror later) |
| `PortAInput` / `PortBInput` | 151-154 | IEC/joy/tape in; keyboard rows/cols |
| `PortAOutputChanged` / `PortBOutputChanged` | 157-160 | IEC ATN, keyboard columns, joy |
| `Ca2State` / `Cb2State` | 619, 653 | IEC CLK/DATA **out** (VIA2 PCR modes) |
| `TriggerCa1` / `TriggerCb1` / `TriggerCa2` / `TriggerCb2` | 555+ | tape / SRQ edges |
| ctor `(IBus, IInterruptLine)` | 117 | pass NMI line for VIA1, IRQ for VIA2 |

Chip stays machine-agnostic; all VIC-20 pin meaning lives in Architectures/Core glue (same rule as C1541: `C1541IecInterfaceDevice`, `C1541DriveMechanismDevice`).

### 2.3 Descriptor patterns to mirror

**C64** (`Architectures/C64/`):

- `C64Descriptor` + `C64RomSet` + profile (`C64MachineProfile`) for clock, video standard, ROM names.
- Device list with roles/base/size (`C64Descriptor.cs:44-65`).
- `ArchitectureBuilder.IsC64Machine` detects VideoChip/CIA/PLA (`ArchitectureBuilder.cs:227-235`) → `BuildC64Machine`.

**C1541** (`Architectures/C1541/`):

- `C1541Descriptor` : `IDriveArchitectureDescriptor` with `DeviceNumber`, `DiskImagePath`, `DosRomName`.
- Devices: 6502 + 2 KB RAM + VIA@$1800 + VIA@$1C00 + 16 KB ROM (`C1541Descriptor.cs:61-68`).
- Builder path independent of host (`BuildC1541Machine`, lines 243-323).

**VIC-20 should mirror C64 host style**: `Vic20Descriptor` (+ optional profile), `Vic20RomSet`, `Vic20ViceRomNames`, dedicated `BuildVic20Machine` (do not piggyback `IsC64Machine`).

**Multisystem**: add `kind == "VIC20"` next to C64/C1541 (`MultiSystemBlueprint.cs:228-235`).

### 2.4 Drive 1540 already catalogued

- `C1541ViceRomNames.Dos1540 = "dos1540-325302+3-01.bin"` (`C1541ViceRomNames.cs:17`).
- `DriveModel.C1540 = 1540` (`DriveModel.cs:16`); in `DriveModelCatalog.Implemented` (`DriveModelCatalog.cs:18-21`).
- Same `C1541Descriptor` with `dosRomName: C1541ViceRomNames.Dos1540`. No new drive architecture needed for default unit 8.

### 2.5 RomFetch VIC20 catalog

`ViceRomCatalog.cs:57-61` already lists:

- Architecture key `"VIC20"`
- kernal / basic / chargen roles (filenames match VICE)
- DRIVES role `"1540"` → `dos1540-325302+3-01.bin` (`:99`)

Need: `IRomProvider` loads under `"VIC20"` (like C64 loader path), and descriptor `RequiredRoms.Architecture = "VIC20"`.

### 2.6 `ViceTopologyBuilder` xvic rejection

```40:43:src/ViceSharp.Launcher/ViceTopologyBuilder.cs
"x128" or "xvic" or "xpet" or ...
    => throw new NotSupportedException(...)
```

Iteration 2 unlock: `"xvic" => BuildVic20Topology(args)` with host `kind: VIC20` and default peripheral drive 8 as C1541 + Dos1540 (or kind that resolves 1540 ROM).

### 2.7 `IVideoChip` / frame assumptions VIC-I must meet

Contract (`IVideoChip.cs`):

- `CurrentRasterLine`, `CyclesPerLine`, `VisibleLines`, `TotalLines`, `IsVBlank`
- `FrameBuffer` BGRA8888, `FrameWidth` / `FrameHeight`, `FrameCompleted`

Host consumption is dimension-agnostic (`VideoServiceHost`, `LocalVideoFrameSource`, `EmulationPumpService` use whatever the chip reports). **No hard-coded 384×272 in the host.**

Caveats:

- VIC-II renderer is fixed **384×272** (`VideoRenderer.cs:11-12`). VIC-I needs its **own** buffer sized for VIC-I geometry (e.g. normal PAL ~224×(311−28+1) with pixel doubling → display width 448 if 2×; or VICE full/debug 284×… / 256×…). Implement under `Chips/VicI/`, not by subclassing VIC-II.
- `DeviceRole.VideoChip` required for pump/UI. VIC-I audio: either also `IAudioChip` + `DeviceRole.AudioChip`, or a thin audio-facing wrapper later.
- VIC-I has **no BA/cycle-steal** like VIC-II; CPU and VIC share the bus differently (half-cycles / character fetches). Do not reuse `ICpuCycleStealer` semantics blindly.

---

## 3. Recommended first skeleton

### 3.1 New types (minimal green path)

**`src/ViceSharp.Architectures/Vic20/`**

| Type | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Vic20ViceRomNames` | Filename constants + `"VIC20"` architecture key |
| `Vic20RomSet` : `IRomSet` | basic + kernal + chargen completeness |
| `Vic20MachineProfile` (+ static presets PAL/NTSC) | clock, lines, cycles/line, ROM picks, ram-block flags |
| `Vic20Descriptor` : `IProfiledArchitectureDescriptor` | device table + `RequiredRoms` |
| Optional: `CommodoreVic20` legacy scaffold (mirror `Commodore64.cs`) only if useful for early unit tests |

Suggested device table (unexpanded PAL):

- `Mos6502` / `DeviceRole.Cpu`
- VIC-I / `VideoChip` @ `$9000` size `$10` (or `$100`)
- VIA1 / new role or reuse a generic “Via” via custom wiring @ `$9110` (NMI)
- VIA2 @ `$9120` (IRQ)
- System RAM (at least `$0000-$03FF` + `$1000-$1FFF`; BLK flags on profile)
- Color RAM `$9400-$97FF` (nybble device)
- Chargen `$8000-$8FFF`, BASIC `$C000-$DFFF`, KERNAL `$E000-$FFFF`

**`src/ViceSharp.Chips/VicI/`** (machine-agnostic)

| Type | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Mos6561` (PAL) / `Mos6560` (NTSC) or one class + TV system | `IVideoChip` (+ optional `IAudioChip` later) |
| Register R/W, raster counters using 71/312 or 65/261 | |
| Stub framebuffer + `FrameCompleted` | enough for host pump |
| Defer accurate matrix fetch / borders / audio | later slices |

**`src/ViceSharp.Core/` (or Vic20-specific wiring next to C64)**

| Type | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Vic20MemoryMap` | flat map + open-bus; no PLA |
| `Vic20IecInterfaceDevice` | VIA1 PA + VIA2 CA2/CB2/CB1 → `IInterSystemBus` |
| `Vic20KeyboardWiring` | VIA2 matrix (can share matrix model with C64 if shapes match) |
| `ArchitectureBuilder.BuildVic20Machine` + `IsVic20Machine` | parallel to C64/C1541 |

**Do not put** keyboard/IEC/tape logic inside `Via6522` or `VicI`.

### 3.2 Default drive 8 = 1540

When building VIC-20 + true drive:

```text
host: Vic20Descriptor (PAL default)
drive 8: C1541Descriptor(
    dosRomName: C1541ViceRomNames.Dos1540,
    deviceNumber: 8,
    diskImagePath: optional)
IEC: Vic20IecInterfaceDevice ↔ existing C1541IecInterfaceDevice / coordinator
```

Reuse 1541 VIA/RAM/ROM substrate; only DOS image and host IEC pinout differ. UI already knows `DriveModel.C1540`.

### 3.3 Integration touchpoints (after skeleton compiles)

1. `ArchitectureBuilder.Build` dispatch for VIC-20  
2. `MultiSystemBlueprint` kind `"VIC20"`  
3. `ViceTopologyBuilder` case `"xvic"`  
4. Console / Xbox machine list enable when ready  
5. Focused tests: ROM load + reset vectors + VIA register smoke + one frame `FrameCompleted`  
6. Lockstep vs `xvic` only after VIC-I cycle model exists  

### 3.4 Suggested slice order (BDP)

1. **Descriptor + memory map + Mos6502 + ROMs** (boots into KERNAL loop if clocks run)  
2. **VIA1/VIA2 map + IRQ/NMI** (timers; keyboard optional)  
3. **VIC-I register + raster timing + empty BGRA frame**  
4. **Keyboard + IEC glue + attach 1540 as unit 8**  
5. **VIC-I character display + color RAM**  
6. **Audio voices, expansions, carts**  

---

## 4. Quick reference: reuse vs new

| Component | Reuse as-is | New / adapt |
|-----------|-------------|-------------|
| CPU | `Mos6502` | none (no port) |
| VIA | `Via6522` | board callbacks only |
| Drive 1540 | `C1541Descriptor` + `Dos1540` | host IEC pinout |
| ROM catalog | `ViceRomCatalog["VIC20"]` | Vic20 loader/descriptor |
| VIC-I | — | new chip under `Chips/VicI` |
| Memory / PLA | — | `Vic20MemoryMap` (no PLA) |
| CIA / SID / VIC-II | C64 only | do not use on VIC-20 |
| Topology `xvic` | reserved throw | implement topology builder |

---
